### paper.tex Sections 5-6 ('exact finite factorizations are supplied with the coefficient and arithmetic certificates'; 'The exact arithmetic checker verifies...')

The cited arithmetic checker and certificates are not in the package. The facts hold by my own exact computation: the support of contact denominators, differences and c/2-theta is exactly Gamma; the residues 59, 97, 109, 108 are nonsquares mod 149; J_* = 30366775457346956958330 < 2^75; the constant C is about 2^299.21 < 2^300; the Euler product over primes <= 1000 outside Gamma is about 2.0397 < 21/10; 220.137 > 219.769; (23/22)log(256036*2^304) is about 233.3 < 240. Include a checker or drop the references.

### research/brox-explicit229-v68/paper.tex lines 1092-1096, 1164-1167, 1180-1183

Short derivations I reconstructed and which could be stated: (a) the pole obstruction follows from the five rows for every prime outside {2,3,17}: (17-e)(3e+17) = 17 b p^2 forces v(e) >= 0 and e = 17 or -17/3 modulo the prime, since 3(17-e)+(3e+17) = 68; then e(17-b) = 17sv makes v(s)+v(v) odd, while (s-17v)(s+51v) = 17 b q^2 needs v(s) = v(v) or q = 0, both impossible. (b) v(I) > 9mu/8 gives order at least two, stronger than the stated one. (c) v_p(Tr(W^{-1})) >= -l holds at inert primes because both conjugates have the same valuation.
items.disposition: v21:five-pole-obstruction and v21:local-extraction: parity, valuation rounding and inert trace derivations

items.text:
### paper.tex lines 429, 538-545, 706-708, 712-717; supplier lines 212-223

Four short steps are used without proof. I reconstructed each. (a) E(M) <= 1 + log M for squarefree M: E(M) = sigma(M)/M is at most the M-th harmonic number. (b) gcd(u,w) = 1 for the selected pair: a common prime would divide every p_{j,theta}, forcing them all equal, which contradicts distinct coefficients. (c) Trace residue 1 or 2 at a selected prime: at the conjugate place each factor is congruent to 1 or has negative valuation, because no nonconstant term can have valuation 0; so the conjugate inverse is 1 or 0 modulo the place. (d) hat_h(P_0) >= 1/2: from h(x(P_0)) = log 41 and the lower duplication inequality, 2 hat_h(P_0) >= log 41 - log(392)/3 > 1.7.
items.disposition: v21:effective-soundness, v21:completeness and v21:finite-sum-height: harmonic bound, gcd, trace residue and canonical-height steps

### paper.tex lines 130-147 (eq:recovery, eq:components) and Section 9.1 (lines 973-1005)

The identification A_j = q^2 S_j rests on the stored-to-physical scalings, which the paper asserts by reference to the parent's substitutions without deriving them at the point of use. Reconstruction from existing material: Version 20 Corollary q198:shifted-aggregate (lines 5169-5197) with Lemma q198:reciprocal-pairs gives the physical row 2(t_0 - t_1) + 14 + (rational part of the sum of x(Q_i)) = 0, where x(Q_i) = s^2 + D(f+g) and x(Q_2) = p. The 196-to-195 passage (v45 paper lines 111-179) is an affine change on x50, x72, x73 only, followed by monomial rescalings by w and C. The byte-verified parent row 175 is 2q(x2 - x86) + 14q^2 + A_0, so matching monomials forces t_j = x_j/q, s = s_st/q, f = C^e f_st/q, g = g_st/q, p_0 = x192/q. Rows 155/156 are the two components of one K-product with identical multipliers, which forces the same scaling for x193. Hence eq:recovery holds componentwise. Recommend adding this derivation or a precise citation at integration.
items.disposition: v21:point-recovery and v21:aggregate-components: both components identified before either aggregate is consumed

### paper.tex lines 429, 626-627, title and abstract

(a) Line 429 uses E(M) <= 1 + log M without proof. It is true: add the primes of M in increasing order and use theta(p) < p log p - 1.
